subject: How to correctly specify a SEM model with experimental treatments and exogenous categorical LV

messages.author: bec3b6c763e426c0
messages.subject: How to correctly specify a SEM model with experimental treatments and exogenous categorical LV
parts:
Hi,

I have a question about how to properly specify a SEM model. For simplicity, assume I have the following variables:

  • Treatment: An experimental manipulation with 3 conditions (control, treatment 1, treatment 2). Specified through 2 dummy variables to represent the two treatments (t1, t2)
  • Gender: An exogenous manifest variable (binary: male, female). Specified through a dummy variable (gen_f)
  • lat1: An exogenous continuous latent variable (with 3 items: x1, x2, x3)
  • lat2: An exogenous categorical latent variable (with 2 items: x4, x5)
  • lat3: An endogenous continuous latent variable (with 3 items: y1, y2, y3) that is regressed on Treatment, Gender, lat1, and lat2
  • lat4: An endogenous continuous latent variable (with 3 items: y4, y5, y6) that is also regressed on Treatment, Gender, lat1, and lat2

Here is the model I specified. I have some questions on this model, as stated below. Thanks in advance.

## Measurement Model

model1 <- 'lat1 =~ x1 + x2 +x3

lat2 =~ x4 + x5

lat3 =~ y1 + y2 +y3

lat4 =~ y4 + y5 +y6

## Structural Model

lat3 ~ t1 + t2 + gen_f + lat1 + lat2

lat4 ~ t1 + t2 + gen_f + lat1 + lat2'

 Questions:

1) Do I need to covary t1 and t2 (the two treatments) as they are dummy variables and thus contain redundant information? i.e.:  t1 ~~ t2

2) Do I need to correlate the other exogenous variables? My understanding is that in the SEM output, only the endogenous LVs are correlated (lat3 with lat4). Why are the exogenous LVs not correlated in SEM as they are in CFA? Do I need to explicitly correlate the predictors (e.g., lat1 ~~ lat2)? Why? Why not?

3) For lat2 (the exogenous categorical LV), do I need to pull it into the latent space and specify it as shown below? Or does this specification apply only to endogenous categorical LV as seems to be suggested here (https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html)? 

lat2 =~ 1*x4 + 1*x5

lat2 ~~ 1*lat2 #fix resid var of latent response var.

x4 ~~ 0*x4 #Or set error variance to x4 variance * (1-reliability)

x5 ~~ 0*x5 #Or set error variance to x5 variance * (1-reliability)

4) What about t1, t2, and gen_f? These are also categorical variables, albeit manifest ones and not LVs (i.e., they are binary dummy variables). Do they need to be pulled into the latent space and specified as follows? I am not sure this would achieve anything, but I was a bit confused about it.

T1 =~ 1*t1

T1 ~~ 1*T1 #fixes resid var of latent response var.

t1 ~~ 0*t1 

T2 =~ 1*t2

T2 ~~ 1*T2

t2 ~~ 0*t2

GEN =~ 1*gen_f

GEN ~~ 1* GEN

gen_f ~~ 0* gen_f

messages.author: 5b9c62b1c7cbc1e6
messages.subject: Re: How to correctly specify a SEM model with experimental treatments and exogenous categorical LV
parts:
Shamel,

First, a clarification. In your model, lat2 is not categorical. It is a continuous latent variable. You don't say explicitly, but I'm guessing from your question that x4 and x5 are categorical, but if so, they are still categorical indicators of a continuous latent.

Most of your other questions can be answered by realizing that the relations among all exogenous variables are unstructured. For most models, you would not specify their covariance in the model syntax nor see it in the output. Explicitly specifying the covariances can have effects you might not anticipate if you're not fully aware of how these things go together.

So:

1) Yes. Leave it to occur by default.

2) Yes. Leave it to occur by default.

3) No. lat2 is, for this purpose, just another exogenous variable. Leave the covariation between lat2 and other exogenous variables to occur by default.

4) You should not specify t1, t2, and gen_f as categorical. Binary variables are a special case--while they are discrete, it's still fine to treat exogenous binary variables as interval. So don't bring them into the model.

So all that said, the first model in your email should be fine (though x4 and x5 may need to specified as categorical).

Hope that helps,
Pat

messages.subject: Re: How to correctly specify a SEM model with experimental treatments and exogenous categorical LV
parts:
Hi Pat,
Thanks very much for your detailed answer. Just to make sure I fully understand it, could you please confirm the points below?
-  “x4 and x5 are categorical, but if so, they are still categorical indicators of a continuous latent” —> Is this because we model categorical indicators by assuming that they depend on continuous latent response variables (X*) weighted by threshold values? 
- “Yes. Leave it to occur by default” —> Do you mean not to specify it in the measurement model and leaving the default option “fixed.x=TRUE” automatically accounts for the covariances among exogenous predictors (by using the original covariance matrix of the observed/ manifest variables)?
- “though x4 and x5 may need to be specified as categorical” —> how do I do this specification? Is there something I need to add/ change in the measurement model code I showed? Or is this done in the data frame of the manifest variables by using the “ordered” argument for these two variables?
Thanks.
Shamel

On Sat, Jul 10, 2021 at 9:27 AM Shamel Addas <shamel...@queensu.ca> wrote:
Hi Pat,
Thanks very much for your detailed answer. Just to make sure I fully understand it, could you please confirm the points below?
-  “x4 and x5 are categorical, but if so, they are still categorical indicators of a continuous latent” —> Is this because we model categorical indicators by assuming that they depend on continuous latent response variables (X*) weighted by threshold values?

Partly. It's more because the assumption in most CFA/SEM is that latent factors are continuous normal variables. Categorical latent variables are generally in the framework of latent class/latent profile models.

- “Yes. Leave it to occur by default” —> Do you mean not to specify it in the measurement model and leaving the default option “fixed.x=TRUE” automatically accounts for the covariances among exogenous predictors (by using the original covariance matrix of the observed/ manifest variables)?

- “though x4 and x5 may need to be specified as categorical” —> how do I do this specification? Is there something I need to add/ change in the measurement model code I showed? Or is this done in the data frame of the manifest variables by using the “ordered” argument for these two variables?

It can be done in either the dataframe or the function call. Either one is sufficient.

Pat

Thanks.
Shamel
